sources.entry: C: _Learn how to write a hash table in C_
Write a hash table in C

summary.one_liner: A tutorial that walks through writing an open-addressed, double-hashed hash table from scratch in C.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a written tutorial rather than a library. It covers hash table structure, hash functions, collision handling, the table's methods, and resizing. It also has an appendix on alternative collision handling. The stated goal is to explain how a hash table works under the hood and when it is and isn't a good choice. The README states the full implementation is around 200 lines of C. It is aimed at readers with some programming and C syntax familiarity. The README does not give run instructions.
use_cases: learning how hash tables work internally
implementing a hash table in C from scratch
studying double hashing and open addressing
understanding when hash tables fail or are a poor fit
practicing low-level C with a data structure project
notable: Implements an open-addressed, double-hashed hash table
Written as a step-by-step tutorial with sections on structure, hashing, collisions, methods and resizing
Includes an appendix on alternative collision handling
Implementation is stated to be around 200 lines of C
caveats: Tutorial rather than a reusable library; no installation or packaging is described
Assumes familiarity with programming and C syntax
README gives no run or build instructions
keywords: when not to use hash table
